samples.summary: Single PR bundles three unrelated design themes plus an unrelated CI-harness test fix
samples.evidence: The change combines (a) backend OAuth `state`/CSRF hardening + CLI loopback nonce (auth.controller.ts, github-auth.guard.ts, cli-auth.store.ts, login.ts), (b) a new CLI URL-building/path-encoding module `packages/cli/src/client/url.ts` with dot-segment rejection applied across ~10 command files, (c) new `--dry-run` support for read commands and api-keys, and (d) an unrelated fix to `scripts/test/changed-areas.test.mjs` (the push-to-main deploy gate). Each is a separately reviewable design decision touching separate design-doc sections (cli.md login flow vs cli.md §8.2 dry-run vs rest-api.md CLI auth endpoints vs the CI harness). No originating issue text was supplied with this review, so I cannot map the bundle to a single stated `outcome`/`acceptance`; if the issue was scoped to the OAuth binding, (b), (c) and (d) are unrequested scope creep, and vice versa.

samples.summary: Browser login is now gated on a process-local in-memory state map; no design doc records the resulting single-instance / restart constraint
samples.evidence: `GitHubAuthGuard.canActivate` now opens a `CliAuthStore` flow for *every* login and `AuthController.githubAuthCallback` refuses any callback whose token it cannot consume. `CliAuthStore` is an in-process `Map` (packages/backend/src/auth/cli-auth.store.ts), so the browser login — previously stateless — now fails whenever the callback lands on a different backend instance than the `/auth/github` request, or after a process restart inside the 5-minute window. rest-api.md's updated bullet still describes the store only as an "in-memory map" and neither it nor backend.md notes the new deployment constraint (grep for `replica|instance|horizontal|scal|in-memory` in docs/design/backend.md returns nothing). Either sticky sessions / a shared store is required, or the trade needs to be stated in the design doc alongside the other risks in the rest-api.md table.

samples.summary: `login` silently changes which server it authenticates against; cli.md's login flow section does not record the new resolution order
samples.evidence: `login` previously read only `--server` (falling back to `DEFAULT_SERVER`); it now calls `getConfig(getGlobalOpts(this))`, so `WAFFLEBASE_SERVER`, an existing session's `server`, and the YAML profile all now steer the login target (packages/cli/src/config/config.ts:77-167). This is a user-visible behaviour change to the auth entry point, but docs/design/cli.md's rewritten "Login flow" section (lines ~170-245) documents only the nonce work and never states the new precedence, even though it references `--server`/`WAFFLEBASE_SERVER` in passing.

samples.summary: New user-facing `--allow-unbound-callback` flag is absent from the canonical command tree (§4)
samples.evidence: §4 "Command Tree" is where every command's flags are enumerated (e.g. `docs export [--format docx|pdf] [--pages] [--force]`), but the `login` entry at line 318 remains bare `login   Browser OAuth login → writes session`. The prose at lines 240-244 argues the flag should be discoverable only via `--help`, which is a reason not to print it in an error message — not a reason to omit it from the design doc's own flag reference.

samples.summary: Stale doc comment on `githubAuth` still names the removed `__cliStateToken` and describes the pre-change CLI-only behaviour
samples.evidence: Lines 89-91 read "For CLI mode, the state token is injected in the guard via __cliStateToken (see below)." The property was renamed to `__oauthStateToken` and the guard now injects it for *every* login, browser included — the comment now describes an API that no longer exists and a policy the change deliberately replaced.

samples.summary: Dry-run branches are inconsistently placed inside vs outside the command's try/catch, giving `seg()` rejections two different error paths
samples.evidence: `docs get` (docs.ts:126), `tabs list` (tabs.ts:15) and `cells get` (cells.ts:21) put the dry-run branch *before* the `try`, so a `seg()` throw escapes `outputError` and propagates out of the action; `api-keys revoke` (api-keys.ts:71), `notes get`, `slides get` and `files get` put theirs inside the `try`, where it is enveloped and sets exit code 1. packages/cli/test/read-dry-run.test.ts encodes both shapes as expected. cli.md §8.1 documents one error envelope and exit-code contract for user errors, so the same invalid identifier should not surface two ways depending on namespace.

finding.summary: Browser login is now gated on a process-local in-memory state map; no design doc records the resulting single-instance / restart constraint
finding.evidence: `GitHubAuthGuard.canActivate` now opens a `CliAuthStore` flow for *every* login and `AuthController.githubAuthCallback` refuses any callback whose token it cannot consume. `CliAuthStore` is an in-process `Map` (packages/backend/src/auth/cli-auth.store.ts), so the browser login — previously stateless — now fails whenever the callback lands on a different backend instance than the `/auth/github` request, or after a process restart inside the 5-minute window. rest-api.md's updated bullet still describes the store only as an "in-memory map" and neither it nor backend.md notes the new deployment constraint (grep for `replica|instance|horizontal|scal|in-memory` in docs/design/backend.md returns nothing). verdict.reason: The claimed code exists exactly as described: GitHubAuthGuard.canActivate creates a store-backed state for the browser path too (github-auth.guard.ts:89-94), AuthController.githubAuthCallback hard-fails any callback whose state it cannot consume for both flows (auth.controller.ts:124-135), and CliAuthStore is a process-local `Map` with a 5-minute TTL (cli-auth.store.ts:24-25, 39). So browser login, previously stateless, now depends on process-local state. The doc gap is also real: rest-api.md:337/351/382 mention only an "in-memory map" and the risk table (which does record other accepted trades at :381, :384, :386) says nothing about a single-instance / restart constraint; docs/design/backend.md has no mention of instances/replicas/scaling/in-memory state (only unrelated eTLD deployment notes at :317, :594), and its Non-Goals (:23-27) do not exclude it. No guard or documented deployment assumption makes this unreachable (docker-compose.yaml declares no replicas, but that is not a stated constraint, and the restart-within-TTL case remains). This falls in the design-fit lane (approach fit for a newly stateful main-path dependency plus design-doc discipline to record the trade in the canonical subsystem doc), so no named refutation ground applies.

finding.summary: Single-use `/start` is at odds with the documented headless copy-paste path it is supposed to preserve
finding.evidence: cli.md:176-178 now says step 3 "Opens (and prints, for copy-paste in headless environments) the nonce-free http://127.0.0.1:<port>/start", and cli.md:206-211 claims "the URL a headless user copies is the same one `open()` is given and the same one that works". Those two properties cannot both hold with a one-shot route: `login` always calls `open(startUrl)` (packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:72) and only falls into the `catch` when the dynamic import or spawn itself throws — `open()` resolves normally in headless/CI environments where a launcher binary exists (xdg-open, `start`, wslview) but no browser ever renders, and browsers can also issue more than one request to a URL (prefetch/preconnect, restored tab). In those cases the first `GET /start` consumes the nonce and the URL the CLI just told the user to visit ("If the browser does not open, visit the URL above.", login.ts:68) answers `410 START_CONSUMED_MESSAGE`, leaving the invocation with no way to complete — a regression against the prior behaviour, which printed a URL that still worked when the browser did not appear. The design doc asserts the property rather than reconciling it (e.g. allowing re-issue until the callback arrives, or only arming single-use after a successful open).
